# Embedded skill: statistical-inference

# Statistical inference

Use the test-selection table, then review before concluding. Do not run fancy stats on every question. Math runs in this pack's `proportion_test.py`.

## Panja runtime

```text
python scripts/proportion_test.py --input /tmp/ab.json
```

Input: `{ "control_success", "control_n", "treatment_success", "treatment_n" }`.  
Output: rates, absolute/relative lift, Wald 95% CI on difference, two-proportion z p-value. Interpret in this skill; do not hand-compute CIs.

## When to load

- Explicit A/B / experiment
- "is this significant"
- Comparing two conversion rates with known n

Otherwise: descriptive + segmentation is enough.

## Test selection

| Data | Test |
|---|---|
| Two proportions (A/B primary) | two-proportion z / `proportion_test.py` |
| Two groups, skewed numeric | Mann-Whitney — say you need scipy; else bootstrap later |
| Categorical association | chi-square (not in this v1 script) |

Always report **effect size + CI + n**, not p alone. Practical vs statistical significance are separate.

## Experiments

Control, treatment, primary metric, guardrails, sample-ratio mismatch, novelty. Do not call a 2-day spike an experiment.

## Review before conclusion (4 rounds, adapted)

1. Wrong test / trivial test / math error
2. Data handling (missing, units, eligible set)
3. Uncertainty present on every headline number
4. Consistency with other results this turn

## STOP

- p-hacking extra slices after seeing p
- Multiple testing without saying so
- Causal claim from an underpowered test
